page.description: openEuler editions and architectures: compare, download official images, or prepare a USB with ROMinit CLI.
page.intro: A free and open source Linux distribution for server, cloud, and edge workloads, with Long Term Support and innovation release lines for x86, AArch64 and RISC-V.
pros: LTS versions carry years-long support windows
cons: The main download pages are behind a JavaScript firewall; images and checksums come from the project's ISO repository instead.
Server-oriented, with a DevStation desktop build on the innovation line.
The everything ISO is 27 GB, so most installs use the standard or netinst image.
page.previewNote: No screenshot with a reusable licence was confirmed for openEuler; the page shows the logo only. No image was written to a USB stick and nothing was booted.
page.status: Write the standard or netinst ISO to a USB stick or attach it to a virtual machine, then install from it. Installing erases the target disk. The LTS line receives security updates while the innovation line ships newer kernels and desktops.
